title: Learned coronary-fat radiomics stratifies an angina-dominated clinical endpoint
summary: A learned coronary-fat radiomics score was associated with subsequent cardiovascular readmissions in 578 prospectively collected patients. The composite endpoint was overwhelmingly worsening or unstable angina, with only two myocardial infarctions. The source reports an adjusted hazard ratio of 2.611 between score-defined groups; cutoff selection in the follow-up cohort and uncertain temporal model locking limit its interpretation as independent prognostic validation.
ai_technology: LASSO radiomics selection and stochastic-gradient-descent classifier of pericoronary fat CT features
organization: Xinjiang Medical University; People’s Hospital of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region

evidence.tested: A matched retrospective development set included 200 event cases and 200 controls, with a random 80:20 split and fivefold cross-validation. LASSO selected fourteen radiomics features and an SGD classifier was selected from five classifiers. A separate prospectively collected cohort included 578 patients with mean follow-up 29.17 months: 129 readmissions for worsening stable or unstable angina and two myocardial infarctions. Events were verified from records/interviews and adjudicated by two blinded cardiovascular specialists. The source reports adjusted HR 2.611, 95% CI 1.806–3.775, for score-defined high versus low groups.
evidence.unknown: The Methods describe ROC-derived cutoffs in the prospective cohort, so the reported risk separation is not a fully independent test of a prespecified threshold. Five-year retrospective outcome ascertainment overlaps the chronology of 2022 validation enrollment; model locking before those outcomes was not established. Matched case-control sampling and a restricted age-based clinical comparator limit calibration and comparative claims. Feature preprocessing isolation is incompletely specified. Single-center data and an angina-dominated composite do not establish broad hard-event prediction, causal inflammation mechanisms or clinical intervention benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised feature selection and the learned radiomics classifier combined CT texture and intensity measurements into the score used for the represented clinical event-association analysis. The segmentation software is labeled AI-assisted by the source, but its undisclosed architecture is not invented here.

source_review.scope: Read original full publisher clinical enrollment/event adjudication, radiomics/learned-classifier and validation Methods, development/later-cohort Results and limitations. Supplements were not independently read. Prospective collection is distinguished from unestablished temporal model/cutoff locking. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
